Thanks — reviewed. Below is the proposed legal counter with rationale. I've kept the MSA protective and scoped the TFC to the OF to limit precedent risk.

Proposed language (MSA):
"Term and Renewal. The Initial Term of the Agreement will be twelve (12) months. Thereafter, this Agreement will automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal no less than sixty (60) days prior to the then-current term's expiration."

Proposed language (Order Form — limited TFC):
"Termination for Convenience (Order Form only). Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the MSA, Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience only after the Initial Term of twelve (12) months by providing thirty (30) days' prior written notice. If Customer exercises this right, Customer will receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid, unused fees. If Customer terminates for convenience prior to completing twenty-four (24) months of service, Customer will pay an early termination fee equal to thirty percent (30%) of the remaining unpaid, committed fees under the Order Form. This Order Form-level termination right shall not amend or create a company-wide right to terminate for convenience under the MSA."

Rationale: 60-day notice on the MSA buys them what they need for budgeting, but we preserve the auto-renew structure and keep uniformity across customers. The OF carveout is narrow and economic (30% fee) to deter opportunistic churn while allowing a measured exit for them. This reduces legal precedent risk.

If Karthik agrees commercially, we'll send as our formal counter and ask StellarTech for a quick confirm or mark-up.

-Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
